text: Re-read at 0.57.2. Comments verified; the emission now records via_attr and bare from whether the callee is a member_expression. JS declares builtin_names for the globals callable with no receiver - deliberately not all of globalThis, only names a method could plausibly collide with. Note JS destructuring (`const {add_row} = obj`) reproduces Python's bound-method-alias hazard, which is exactly why the rule is restricted to language-defined names rather than to bare calls in general.
